objective: Factor the canonical fitted scalar syndrome supports through a compact outcome-independent bank of symmetric bilinear component invariants and test how much rank-phase grading is actually required.
frozen_component_bits: remaining local capacity low two bits
per-owner residuals touching the current frontier parity
per-owner frontier-column and touched-column count parity
cross-owner shared touched/frontier column count parity
per-owner delay-bin cell parity for depth 0, depth 1, and depth >=2
pair_construction: For each unordered pair of odd component types, form all symmetric bilinear products of the frozen binary component features and XOR-aggregate identical products.
phase_modes: GLOBAL: one coefficient per bilinear invariant across ranks within a carrier
R3: coefficients graded by rank mod 3
R6: coefficients graded by rank mod 6
EXACT: coefficients graded by exact rank
frozen_from_prior: two-dimensional scalar target quotient on demanding carriers
anti_circularity: All component bits and phase modes are declared before outcome qualification.
No W/D/L label selects or modifies a candidate feature.
Exact component identities remain only in the already-frozen affine part; the new interaction bank is structurally compressed.
falsifiers: Any contradiction rejects that phase mode for this candidate bank on the tested carrier.
If EXACT fails, these simple binary invariants are insufficient even with exact-rank grading.
A pass does not establish cross-geometry coefficient transfer; that requires a subsequent frozen-coefficient test.
next_if_success: Choose the coarsest phase mode exact on every demanding carrier, extract deterministic syndrome coefficients, then test coefficient transfer on a predeclared fresh non-affine carrier.
next_if_fail: Enrich the bank only with independently motivated REL_INC topology invariants suggested by support factorization; do not add outcome-selected features.
